messages:
sasha: Quick thread — follow-up on the credential contract shrinkwrap we discussed in the RFC. Goal: a minimal, backward-compatible surface to onboard operator tooling and platform teams without widening the key surface. Looking for tradeoffs + rollout plan. cc @aj @maria

aj: Ack. high-level: prefer small delta for runtime -> fewer fallback paths. What's the wire shape you want?

sasha: Proposal sketch: normalize to a single header that encodes type+payload. Runtime normalizes into internal actor claims. Examples:
```
# legacy
Authorization: Redwood abcdefg-legacy-key

# new (single header)
X-Redwood-Auth: type=api_key;payload=ak_....;scope=project:123
```
This lets us parse and short-circuit into existing authn pipeline.

maria: I like a single header for parsing simplicity. Concern: telemetry + IAM mapping must preserve original token type so audits don't lose context. Also need explicit ttl for ephemeral tokens.

sasha: agreed. runtime will attach metadata: origin=(legacy|new), ttl, source_ip in audit events.

tim: How about backward compat window? Platform teams will take time to rotate. If we deprecate legacy too fast they won't be able to cutover.

sasha: thinking: accept both for 90 days, emit deprecation audit/log warning when legacy seen, and a rate-limited banner in the console for keys > 90 days old. After 90 days we enter 2-stage: first: read-only reject for new writes, second: full reject at 180 days. Thoughts?

aj: 90/180 seems reasonable. Ops note: we need to ensure Dedicated/private customers can opt into longer windows or extensions via support ticket.

maria: RBAC mapping question — the new header includes "scope" but we should not let that be the source of truth for permissions. Must map to claims in our identity service and validate against project/org graph. Avoid trusting arbitrary scope fields coming from clients.

sasha: yep — "scope" is just a hint to help routing and visibility, not an assertion. runtime will exchange key -> actor_id -> roles via authz service for policy evaluation.

tim: For operator onboarding, we need ephemeral tokens for bootstrap flows. Proposal: short-lived bootstrap tokens minted by the control plane with a one-time exchange to long-lived api_key scoped to admin:operator role. That avoids embedding platform secrets in images.

sasha: good. add requirement: exchange audit trail + single-use nonce to prevent replay.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: New feature flag created: auth.header_unified_enabled (off by default in production clusters).

aj: rollout plan: 1) server accepts new header but default remains legacy; 2) enable canary in staging for two weeks; 3) enable opt-in in Dedicated customers; 4) flip in hosted for low-traffic routes; 5) turn on deprecation warnings; 6) full enforcement after 90/180 windows. Each step gated by telemetry checks (error rate, latency bump, auth failures).

maria: Tests: unit parsing tests, fuzz unknown header shapes, authz contract tests (mapping to roles), e2e including private deployment where KMS-backed key material used. We also need addon: a migration lint that flags services still sending legacy header.

sasha: Add monitoring hooks: percentage of requests using legacy vs new header, per-route auth failure rate, latency percentiles for auth negotiation, audit event volume. Rollback safepoint defined: if auth failures > 0.5% above baseline for 10m, revert new header parsing rollout.

tim: Edgecases: 1) proxy/brokered keys where downstream loses original header; 2) services that rely on header ordering or raw header content in logs; 3) signed webhook payloads that include legacy signature scheme. Need compatibility shims or explicit migration docs.

sasha: For proxy cases, plan to expose a small shim library and nginx sidecar snippet for header preservation and translation. Example snippet for sidecar config included in the migration doc.

aj: Implementation notes: parse in gateway layer, attach normalized claim bag to request context, short-circuit old code paths to read normalized bag. Keep parsing idempotent and cheap (avoid crypto on each request; cache token->claims mapping with TTL).

maria: Cache TTL tradeoff: lower TTL means faster revocation but higher load on identity service. Suggest default 5m with ability to lower to 30s for high-sensitivity routes. Documented per-route override in route config.

sasha: Security checklist before flip: key rotation APIs available, audited exchange path, KMS integration for private deploys, automated lint for legacy use, canary metrics dashboard. Assign owners?

aj: I'll own gateway parsing + canary rollout. tim will own shim sidecar and operator onboarding flow. maria owns authz mapping tests and migration lint. sasha will coordinate docs + console deprecation messages.

infra-bot: reminder: created ticket ENGSEC-1284 with the rollout checklist and canary dashboards.

sasha: Thanks all. I'll draft the rollout playbook and post link here when ready. If anyone sees any missing show-stoppers call out now. :thumbsup:

pm: (note: thread closed)
